content: The text provided is a highly detailed and technical document, primarily focused on aircraft disinsection procedures, aircraft models, and their respective specifications. Aircraft disinsection involves the application of insecticides to prevent the spread of vector-borne diseases. The process is carried out using specific chemical agents, such as 2% permethrin or 2% d-phenothrin (or its isomer, 1R-trans-phenothrin). These agents may be applied individually or in combination, depending on the aircraft type and operational requirements. Aircraft Models and Disinsection Requirements: 1. Boeing Aircraft: Boeing 737 Series: Models such as the 737-100, 737-200, and 737-800 require disinsection in the cabin, forward hold, and aft hold. The application rate is specified in grams per hold. Boeing 747 Series: The 747-100, 747-200, and 747-400 models require disinsection in the main deck cargo area, forward hold, and aft hold. Residual disinsection products must be reapplied every 8 weeks or after significant cleaning operations. Boeing 777 and 787: These long-haul aircraft require similar disinsection protocols, with specific attention to the cabin and cargo holds. 2. Regional and Private Aircraft: Bombardier CRJ Series: The CRJ-200 and CRJ-900 models require disinsection in the cabin and holds. Smaller jets, such as the Challenger series, may not require hold disinsection due to their design. Embraer E-Jets: Models like the Embraer 170 and 190 require disinsection in the cabin and holds, with specified application rates for permethrin and d-phenothrin. 3. Military Aircraft: Military aircraft, such as the Airbus KC-30 (A330 MRTT) and Lockheed C-130 Hercules, may require disinsection in the cabin and holds. However, fighter jets are typically exempt due to their sensitive electronic equipment and low risk of carrying live mosquitoes. 4. Freighter Aircraft: Freighter models, including the Airbus A300-600ST Beluga and Antonov An-124, require disinsection in the main deck cargo area, forward hold, and aft hold. Application rates are specified for each section. Disinsection Procedures: Cabin Pre-Embarkation: Insecticides are applied before passengers board the aircraft to ensure the cabin is free of vectors. Cabin Pre-Departure or On-Arrival: Additional disinsection may be performed before departure or upon arrival, depending on the destination's health regulations. Cargo Holds: Forward and aft holds are treated with insecticides at specified rates to prevent the transport of vectors in cargo. Chemical Agents: Permethrin 2%: A synthetic pyrethroid used for its long-lasting residual effect. d-Phenothrin 2%: Another synthetic pyrethroid, often used in combination with permethrin for enhanced efficacy. 1R-trans-Phenothrin: An isomer of d-phenothrin, used interchangeably in some formulations. International Standards: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) provides guidelines for aircraft disinsection, in accordance with World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations. These standards are outlined in Annex 9 of the ICAO's Facilitation Manual. Disinsection certificates must be renewed every 8 weeks or after cleaning operations that remove residual insecticides. Health Considerations: Crew members are trained to identify passengers displaying symptoms of communicable diseases, such as persistent coughing, impaired breathing, or skin rashes. These cases are reported to health authorities, and appropriate measures are taken to prevent disease transmission. Documentation: Aircraft operators must maintain detailed records of all disinsection treatments, including the date, time, location, and method of application. These records are essential for compliance with international health regulations.
